title: A `match` with two `default` arms compiles, and so does a `switch` with two `default` labels.
text: `match ($n) { default => "first", 1 => "one", default => "second" }` compiles and gives `"first"` for every subject but `1`, so the second `default` can never run and nothing says so. A `switch` with two `default:` labels compiles too, and runs the first. It closes when a second `default` in either is a compile error where it is written, with a conformance case.
